notes.summary: History gives about 3–4 questions in SSC CGL. Most come from the Indus Valley, Buddhism and Jainism, the Mauryas and Guptas, the Delhi Sultanate and Mughals, and the freedom struggle (1857–1947). Learn who, where and when for each big event.

concepts.title: Ancient India: Indus Valley to the Guptas
concepts.body:
• Indus Valley (Harappan) Civilisation: Bronze Age, town planning with grid streets and covered drains. Harappa was excavated first by Daya Ram Sahni (1921); Mohenjo-daro by R.D. Banerji (1922). The Great Bath is at Mohenjo-daro; a dockyard at Lothal (Gujarat).
  • Buddha: born at Lumbini, enlightenment at Bodh Gaya, first sermon at Sarnath, death (mahaparinirvana) at Kushinagar.
  • Mahavira was the 24th Jain tirthankara; Rishabhanatha was the first.
  • Maurya Empire: founded by Chandragupta Maurya with the help of Chanakya (Kautilya, author of the Arthashastra). Megasthenes wrote Indica. Ashoka turned to Buddhism after the Kalinga war.
  • Gupta Empire: called the 'Golden Age'. Aryabhata (astronomer) and Kalidasa (poet) belong to this period.

concepts.title: Medieval India: Sultanate and Mughals
concepts.body:
RulerRemember for
Qutb-ud-din AibakFounder of Slave (Mamluk) dynasty; began the Qutub Minar
IltutmishCompleted Qutub Minar; introduced silver tanka and copper jital
Alauddin KhiljiMarket control reforms
Muhammad bin TughlaqToken currency; shifted capital from Delhi to Daulatabad
BaburFounded Mughal Empire after First Battle of Panipat (1526)
AkbarDin-i-Ilahi, Mansabdari system, Second Battle of Panipat (1556)

concepts.title: Modern India: the freedom struggle
concepts.body:
• 1857: Revolt began at Meerut.
  • 1885: Indian National Congress founded by A.O. Hume; first session at Bombay, president W.C. Bonnerjee.
  • 1905: Partition of Bengal by Lord Curzon; Swadeshi movement.
  • 1919: Rowlatt Act; Jallianwala Bagh massacre at Amritsar (13 April).
  • 1920: Non-Cooperation Movement (withdrawn after Chauri Chaura, 1922).
  • 1930: Dandi (Salt) March, start of Civil Disobedience.
  • 1942: Quit India Movement ('Do or Die').
  • 1947: Independence on 15 August.

varieties.name: Ancient India facts
varieties.how: Link each site or person to one key fact (place, discoverer, book).

example.q: Where did Gautama Buddha deliver his first sermon?

varieties.name: Medieval rulers and their works
varieties.how: Use the ruler table: one famous reform or building per ruler.

steps: Token currency of copper/bronze is linked with the Tughlaq experiments
Muhammad bin Tughlaq also moved the capital to Daulatabad

varieties.name: Freedom struggle and chronology
varieties.how: Memorise the timeline of years; for order questions write the year next to each event first.

example.q: Arrange: Quit India, Dandi March, Partition of Bengal.
example.answer: Partition of Bengal, Dandi March, Quit India

tips: For chronology questions, write the year beside each option event before comparing.
Buddha's four places in order of life: Lumbini, Bodh Gaya, Sarnath, Kushinagar (L-B-S-K).
Viceroy questions usually ask the event linked to the name; learn them in pairs.
traps: Harappa (Daya Ram Sahni, 1921) and Mohenjo-daro (R.D. Banerji, 1922) are often swapped in options.
Qutub Minar was begun by Aibak but completed by Iltutmish.
The first session of INC was presided by W.C. Bonnerjee, not by A.O. Hume, who founded it.

questions.q: Who led the first excavation at Harappa in 1921?
questions.solution:
Harappa was first excavated by Daya Ram Sahni in 1921 (under John Marshall as ASI Director-General). R.D. Banerji excavated Mohenjo-daro in 1922.
Memory hook: Harappa came first, so the first name, Sahni, goes with 1921.

questions.q: The Mughal Empire in India was founded after which battle?
questions.solution:
Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi in the First Battle of Panipat (1526) and founded the Mughal Empire.
Memory hook: 1526: Babur's 'first' Panipat = first Mughal.

questions.q: Who presided over the first session of the Indian National Congress (1885)?
questions.solution:
The first INC session was held at Bombay in 1885 and was presided over by W.C. Bonnerjee. A.O. Hume was the founder.
Memory hook: Hume founded, Bonnerjee presided.

questions.q: Which ruler adopted Buddhism after the Kalinga war?
questions.solution:
The bloodshed of the Kalinga war (c. 261 BCE) moved Ashoka to adopt Buddhism and follow Dhamma.
Memory hook: Kalinga changed Ashoka from 'Chandashoka' (fierce) to 'Dharmashoka'.

questions.q: Which Delhi Sultan shifted his capital from Delhi to Daulatabad?
questions.solution:
Muhammad bin Tughlaq moved the capital to Daulatabad (Devagiri) and also issued token currency. Both experiments failed.
Memory hook: Muhammad bin Tughlaq = 'ideas ahead of time': token money and a new capital.

questions.q: In which year did the Jallianwala Bagh massacre take place?
questions.solution:
The massacre took place at Amritsar on 13 April 1919 (Baisakhi day) under General Dyer, after protests against the Rowlatt Act.
Memory hook: Rowlatt Act and Jallianwala are both 1919.

questions.q:
Arrange in chronological order:
1. Quit India Movement
2. Partition of Bengal
3. Dandi March
4. Jallianwala Bagh massacre
questions.solution:
Partition of Bengal 1905 → Jallianwala Bagh 1919 → Dandi March 1930 → Quit India 1942. So 2, 4, 3, 1.
Memory hook: 05 – 19 – 30 – 42: each gap grows by about a decade.

questions.q: Which pair is incorrectly matched (place — event in Buddha's life)?
questions.solution:
Kushinagar is where Buddha attained mahaparinirvana (death). Enlightenment was at Bodh Gaya.
Memory hook: L-B-S-K follows his life: born, enlightened, taught, passed away.
